necessary_context.content: For each arm i, successive rewards X_{i,s}, s>=1, are iid with unknown law P_i and mean mu_i. Rewards across different arms are independent. A policy chooses the next arm from past plays and observed rewards; T_i(n) counts its plays in the first n rounds.
necessary_context.name: Reward sequences and feedback

necessary_context.content: mu*=max_i mu_i; Delta_i=mu*-mu_i. Expected regret R_n=n mu* - sum_i mu_i E[T_i(n)]. Theorem 1 assumes all P_i have support in [0,1].
necessary_context.locator: PDF p.2 / p.236 regret definition; PDF p.3 / p.237 gap definition and Theorem 1
necessary_context.name: Expected regret and gaps

necessary_context.content: Fact 1 states that [0,1]-valued X_t with E[X_t|X_1,...,X_{t-1}]=mu satisfy P(S_m>=m mu+a)<=exp(-2a^2/m) and the analogous lower tail for a>=0. The UCB1 Proof applies this to fixed-length arm sample prefixes.
necessary_context.locator: PDF p.8 / p.242, Fact 1 and Proof of Theorem 1
necessary_context.name: Concentration dependency
